config.title: Tab-Based App Shell

intro.title: Tab-Based App Shell
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a mobile app with a tab-based navigation shell using Ionic and Angular. You will learn how to structure an app with multiple views accessible via bottom tabs. The core concept is using Ionic's tab components and Angular routing to manage different sections of the app. You will work with Ionic's UI components, Angular modules, and Capacitor for native mobile features. By the end, you'll have a functional app shell that users can navigate by tapping on tabs.
intro.usecase: Tab-based navigation is a fundamental pattern in mobile apps where users need to switch between distinct functional areas quickly. You'll see this in apps like Instagram (Home, Search, Reels, Activity, Profile), banking apps (Accounts, Transfers, Payments, Support), and productivity tools like Slack (Chats, Channels, Mentions, You). As a developer, implementing a tab shell with Ionic provides the foundation for organizing complex app functionality into intuitive sections while maintaining smooth navigation transitions and consistent UI patterns across platforms.

objectives: Apply the Ionic CLI to generate a new tab-based application shell.
Utilize Angular routing to define navigation paths for each tab.
Construct an Ionic tab bar component to serve as the primary navigation interface.
Implement tab-specific page components to display distinct content areas.
Define and assign routes within the main application routing module to connect tabs to their pages.
Use the Angular router-outlet directive to control the display of active tab content.
Execute the application in a browser to verify the tab navigation structure functions.
Modify the tab bar configuration to customize icons and labels for each navigation item.
Handle tab selection events to manage UI state and content updates.
Access and utilize Capacitor's native platform APIs to prepare the shell for mobile device deployment.
Store and retrieve navigation state to maintain the active tab across user sessions.
Compare the structure of a tab-based shell with other navigation patterns to reinforce architectural understanding.

steps.title: Import Ionic Angular core components
steps.instruction: Import the Ionic UI components needed for building the tab interface: IonTabs, IonTabBar, IonTabButton, IonIcon, IonLabel, and IonRouterOutlet from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement with curly braces to import all the listed components from the '@ionic/angular' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing Ionic components
import { IonButton, IonContent, IonHeader } from '@ionic/angular';
steps.seedCode:
// Import Ionic Angular core components for tab interface
// Add your import statement here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement will be added, making the Ionic tab components available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The code should include an import statement that imports IonTabs, IonTabBar, IonTabButton, IonIcon, IonLabel, and IonRouterOutlet from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Ionic tab components. These will be essential for building your tab-based app shell.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some components, but you're missing one or more of the required ones: IonTabs, IonTabBar, IonTabButton, IonIcon, IonLabel, and IonRouterOutlet. Make sure to import all of them from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import IonTabs, IonTabBar, IonTabButton, IonIcon, IonLabel, and IonRouterOutlet from '@ionic/angular'.

steps.title: Import Angular routing modules
steps.instruction: Import RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router' to enable routing functionality for your tab navigation.
steps.hint: Add an import statement that brings in both RouterModule and Routes from the '@angular/router' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Import Angular routing modules
import { RouterModule, Routes } from '@angular/router';
steps.expectedOutcome: The RouterModule and Routes are imported from '@angular/router', making them available for setting up tab routing.
successCriteria: The import statement should include both RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported RouterModule and Routes, which are essential for Angular routing in your tab-based app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the import statement needs both RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'. Check that you've included both.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.

steps.title: Import Ionic icons
steps.instruction: Import the add, albums, and person icons from 'ionicons/icons' to use in the tab buttons.
steps.hint: Use named imports from 'ionicons/icons' to get the specific icon symbols you need.
steps.analogousExample:
// Import specific icons for tab buttons
import { add, albums, person } from 'ionicons/icons';
steps.expectedOutcome: The icons are imported and ready to be used in the tab buttons.
successCriteria: The import statement includes add, albums, and person from 'ionicons/icons'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the icons needed for the tab buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing all three icons (add, albums, person) from 'ionicons/icons'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import the add, albums, and person icons from 'ionicons/icons'.

steps.title: Create the main tab component
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class with the @Component decorator and set standalone: true. Name the component class 'TabsPage'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' and define a class with the name TabsPage. Set standalone to true in the decorator configuration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A standalone Angular component class named TabsPage is created with the @Component decorator.
successCriteria: The code must include a class named TabsPage decorated with @Component, and the decorator configuration must include standalone: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TabsPage component with standalone: true. This is the foundation for our tab-based app shell.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but something is missing. Make sure you have: 1) A class named TabsPage, 2) The @Component decorator, and 3) standalone: true in the decorator configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. You need to define a class named TabsPage with the @Component decorator and set standalone: true.

steps.title: Define component imports
steps.instruction: Add the imports array to the @Component decorator with IonicModule, CommonModule, and RouterModule.
steps.hint: Look for the @Component decorator and add the imports property with an array containing the three modules.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component decorator now includes an imports array with IonicModule, CommonModule, and RouterModule.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator must have an imports property containing an array with IonicModule, CommonModule, and RouterModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've properly configured the component imports. This allows the component to use Ionic components, common Angular directives, and routing functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added all three required modules: IonicModule, CommonModule, and RouterModule in the imports array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component decorator needs an imports array with IonicModule, CommonModule, and RouterModule. Check that you've added the imports property correctly.

steps.title: Define tab routes configuration
steps.instruction: Inside the @Component decorator, add an 'imports' array that includes RouterModule.
steps.hint: The imports array goes inside the @Component decorator configuration object, after the selector property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component metadata now includes RouterModule in its imports array, enabling routing functionality.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator should have an imports property containing [RouterModule].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added RouterModule to the component's imports. This enables the routing features needed for tab navigation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added an 'imports' array inside the @Component decorator that contains RouterModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component still needs RouterModule imported. Add an 'imports' array with [RouterModule] inside the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Initialize the template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template property to the @Component decorator that returns the basic Ionic tabs structure: an <ion-tabs> component containing an <ion-router-outlet> and an <ion-tab-bar>.
steps.hint: The template should be a string starting and ending with backticks (`). Inside, include the two Ionic components in order.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TabsComponent now has a template property with the basic Ionic tabs structure containing ion-router-outlet and ion-tab-bar components.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with backticks containing <ion-tabs>, <ion-router-outlet>, and <ion-tab-bar> elements in the correct order.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the basic Ionic tabs template structure. The <ion-router-outlet> will display the tab content, and the <ion-tab-bar> will contain the navigation buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your template includes all required elements: <ion-tabs> as the wrapper, <ion-router-outlet> for content, and <ion-tab-bar> for navigation. Also ensure the template uses backticks (`) for multi-line strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Remember to add a template property to the @Component decorator with backticks containing <ion-tabs>, <ion-router-outlet>, and <ion-tab-bar> elements.

steps.title: Add router outlet for tab content
steps.instruction: Inside the IonTabs component in your template, add an IonRouterOutlet component with the router outlet directive.
steps.hint: The IonRouterOutlet should be placed inside IonTabs and use Angular's router outlet directive to display routed content.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding router outlet inside tabs
<ion-tabs>
  <ion-router-outlet></ion-router-outlet>
  <!-- Tab bar will go here -->
</ion-tabs>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes an IonRouterOutlet inside the IonTabs component, which will display the content for each tab route.
successCriteria: The IonRouterOutlet component should be added inside the IonTabs element in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the IonRouterOutlet component inside the IonTabs. This will serve as the container where the content for each tab route will be displayed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the IonRouterOutlet is placed directly inside the IonTags component and uses the correct Angular directive.
steps.feedbackWrong: The IonRouterOutlet component needs to be added inside the IonTabs element. Check that you're using the correct Ionic component name and Angular directive syntax.

steps.title: Create the tab bar container
steps.instruction: Inside the ion-tabs element in your template, add an ion-tab-bar element with the slot attribute set to 'bottom'.
steps.hint: The ion-tab-bar should be placed after the router outlet comment but still inside the ion-tabs element. Use the slot attribute to position it at the bottom of the tabs.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Inside an ion-tabs template -->
<ion-tabs>
  <ion-router-outlet></ion-router-outlet>
  <ion-tab-bar slot="bottom">
    <!-- Tab buttons will go here -->
  </ion-tab-bar>
</ion-tabs>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains an ion-tab-bar element positioned at the bottom of the tabs, ready to hold tab buttons.
successCriteria: The ion-tab-bar element is present inside ion-tabs, has the slot="bottom" attribute, and is placed after the router outlet.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the tab bar container. This will hold the tab buttons that users can tap to navigate between different sections of your app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the ion-tab-bar element inside the ion-tags element, and that it has the slot="bottom" attribute to position it correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tab bar container wasn't added correctly. You need to add an ion-tab-bar element with slot="bottom" inside the ion-tabs element in your template.

steps.title: Add first tab button
steps.instruction: Inside the <ion-tab-bar> element, add the first tab button for 'tab1' with the 'person' icon and 'Profile' label. Use the imported IonTabButton, IonIcon, and IonLabel components.
steps.hint: Add an <ion-tab-button> element with tab='tab1' and routerLink='/tabs/tab1'. Inside it, place an <ion-icon> with name='person' and an <ion-label> with 'Profile' text.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of a tab button structure -->
<ion-tab-button tab="tab1" routerLink="/tabs/tab1">
  <ion-icon name="person"></ion-icon>
  <ion-label>Profile</ion-label>
</ion-tab-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The tab bar now contains the first tab button with a person icon and 'Profile' label that will navigate to the 'tab1' route.
successCriteria: The code must include an <ion-tab-button> element with tab='tab1' and routerLink='/tabs/tab1', containing an <ion-icon> with name='person' and an <ion-label> with text 'Profile'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added the first tab button with the correct structure and attributes. This creates a functional tab navigation element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but check: 1) Does the <ion-tab-button> have both tab='tab1' and routerLink='/tabs/tab1'? 2) Is the <ion-icon> using name='person'? 3) Does the <ion-label> contain 'Profile' text?
steps.feedbackWrong: The tab button structure is missing or incorrect. Remember to use <ion-tab-button> with tab and routerLink attributes, containing <ion-icon> and <ion-label> elements inside.

steps.title: Add second tab button
steps.instruction: Add a second IonTabButton inside the ion-tab-bar element, after the first tab button. Set its tab attribute to 'tab2', routerLink to '/tabs/tab2', and use the settings icon.
steps.hint: Copy the structure of the first tab button but change the icon to 'settings' and update the tab and routerLink values.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding a second tab button -->
<ion-tab-button tab="tab2" routerLink="/tabs/tab2">
  <ion-icon [icon]="settings"></ion-icon>
  <ion-label>Settings</ion-label>
</ion-tab-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The tab bar now has two tab buttons: the first with an add icon linking to tab1, and the second with a settings icon linking to tab2.
successCriteria: The code should contain a second IonTabButton element with tab="tab2", routerLink="/tabs/tab2", and the settings icon used in its ion-icon.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the second tab button with the settings icon. This creates a second navigation option in your tab-based app shell.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a second tab button, but it's missing one or more required attributes. Make sure it has tab="tab2", routerLink="/tabs/tab2", and uses the settings icon.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second tab button is missing or incorrect. Add an IonTabButton element inside the ion-tab-bar with the specified attributes and icon.

steps.title: Add third tab button
steps.instruction: Add the third tab button inside the ion-tab-bar, using the person icon imported earlier. The button should have tab='tab3' and routerLink='/tabs/tab3'.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the first tab button. Use ion-tab-button with tab, routerLink, ion-icon, and ion-label.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of a third tab button -->
<ion-tab-button tab="tab3" routerLink="/tabs/tab3">
  <ion-icon [icon]="person"></ion-icon>
  <ion-label>Profile</ion-label>
</ion-tab-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The tab bar now has three tab buttons: Add, Settings, and Profile.
successCriteria: The third ion-tab-button must have tab='tab3', routerLink='/tabs/tab3', use the person icon, and display a label like 'Profile'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've completed the tab bar with all three buttons. The tab-based navigation shell is now fully functional.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a third tab button, but check: does it have tab='tab3', routerLink='/tabs/tab3', the person icon, and a label?
steps.feedbackWrong: The third tab button is missing or incorrect. Add an ion-tab-button with tab='tab3', routerLink='/tabs/tab3', using the person icon and a label.
